findings.summary: The left panel's four bars total 215.2 per cent (99.1 + 67.5 + 31.4 + 17.2) of the same 6,088,067 bytes, because each stub is lowered from the unstubbed program and the stubs overlap — the corner-height Hessian sits inside the derivative tower, and the value-path stub removes everything. Nothing on the panel or in the caption says the rows are independent measurements rather than a partition, so a reader who adds the bars, which the shared percentage axis invites, gets more than the whole. The head's new graph table in the evidence fragment gives the same rows as raw bytes and shares but also carries no additivity note.

The legend's dotted swatch for the erased state denotes a mark that appears nowhere in the picture: the erased row's bar is drawn with zero length at the axis, so no dotted outline is rendered in either panel while the legend displays one. The legend's own words ('zero-length bar, marked in text, no share') and the row's text carry the meaning, which is why the reader is not stopped.

The canvas is drawn 17.6 in wide, above the 14-in full-width canvas the project's figure style specifies. At the delivered 1400 px width the 14 pt labels render about 15.5 px tall instead of the calibrated 19.4 px, so this figure's text sits roughly 20 per cent smaller than every other nova figure on a page, and the rotated span labels (11.5 pt, figure.py:177) — which carry the 119.2 s and 189.6 s the record's prose quotes — are the smallest text in the set. All text is legible in the render, so this does not hold the node.
